3-4: Listen carefully and identify everyday sounds around them, such as birds, traffic and water.
Hear and say words that rhyme and join in with rhyming songs.
Clap the beats (syllables) in names and familiar words.
Hear and say the first sound in familiar words, such as 's' in sun.
Recognise the letters s, a, t and p and say their sounds.
Recognise the letters i, n, m and d and say their sounds.
Blend spoken sounds together to hear a word, such as c-a-t makes cat.
Recognise their own name in print and say the first letter.
Hold a book the right way, turn pages one at a time and know that print carries meaning.
Retell a familiar story in the right order using pictures and props.
Name the characters in a story and say something about them.
Guess what might happen next in a story and explain why.
Learn and use new words from stories and from places they visit.
Use simple describing words for colour, size and feeling.
Ask who, what and where questions about things they see and hear.
Talk about their day using sentences of four to six words.
Follow two-step instructions, such as 'pick up the shell and put it in the bucket'.
Learn and perform a few nursery rhymes and songs from memory.
Make marks, lines and circles with crayons, chalk or a stick in the sand.
Hold a pencil or crayon with a comfortable grip and draw controlled lines.
Draw zigzags, waves and loops as pre-writing patterns.
Attempt to write the first letter of their name, then the whole name.
Notice print in the environment, such as shop signs, menus and tickets.
Describe what is happening in a picture or photograph.
Name feelings like happy, sad, scared and excited in themselves and in story characters.
Know and use pairs of opposites such as hot/cold, up/down and wet/dry.
Find objects that start with a given sound around where the family is staying.
Make up a short story with a beginning and an end using toys or found objects.
Listen to a short poem and talk about the words and sounds they liked.
Learn words for transport, places and things seen on the journey.
5-6: Read words with common digraphs such as sh, ch, th, ng and ck.
Blend sounds to read consonant-vowel-consonant words like dog, map and sun.
Read words with adjacent consonants such as frog, stamp and crisp.
Read words with vowel digraphs such as ai, ee, oa, oo and igh.
Read words with split digraphs such as a-e in cake and i-e in kite.
Read common exception words such as the, said, was and they.
Spell simple words by segmenting them into sounds.
Spell the days of the week correctly.
Form lower-case letters correctly, starting and finishing in the right place.
Form capital letters and use them for names, places and the word I.
Leave spaces between words when writing.
Year 1 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Begin a sentence with a capital letter and end it with a full stop.
Year 1 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Use question marks and exclamation marks to show questions and surprise.
Year 1 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Join words and ideas in a sentence using 'and'.
Year 1 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Say a sentence out loud before writing it, then read it back to check.
Write two or three sentences about a place they visited, as on a postcard.
Write a short recount of a trip using first, next and then.
Listen to stories and talk about favourite parts and characters.
Retell well-known fairy and traditional tales, including one from the country they are in.
Predict what might happen next from what has been read so far.
Explain why something happened in a story using events from the text.
Learn a short poem by heart and say it aloud with expression.
Find information in a simple non-fiction book using pictures and labels.
Use adjectives to describe people, places and things.
Year 1 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Add -s or -es to make plurals, such as dogs and boxes.
Use the prefix un- to change the meaning of words, such as unhappy and undo.
Write labels and captions for drawings, photos and maps.
Speak in front of others about an object found on their travels.
Read simple words on signs, menus and tickets in English-speaking settings.
7-9: Add suffixes such as -ment, -ness, -ful, -less and -ly and spell the new words.
Use prefixes such as dis-, mis-, re- and pre- to change meaning.
Spell and use common homophones such as there/their/they're and to/too/two.
Use apostrophes in contractions such as can't, didn't and it's.
Year 2 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Use apostrophes to show possession, such as the girl's hat and the girls' hats.
Year 4 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Use commas to separate items in a list.
Year 2 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Use conjunctions such as when, if, because and although to join clauses.
Year 3 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Write expanded noun phrases, such as the tall, crumbling tower by the sea.
Year 2 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Use the past and present tense correctly and consistently.
Year 2 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Start sentences with fronted adverbials followed by a comma, such as 'Early that morning,'.
Year 4 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Punctuate direct speech using inverted commas.
Year 4 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Organise writing into paragraphs around a theme.
Join letters neatly and consistently in handwriting.
Write a diary entry about a real day using first person and past tense.
Write a letter to a friend or relative describing a place, with greeting and sign-off.
Write clear instructions with imperative verbs and numbered steps, such as a local recipe.
Describe a real place using the five senses and vivid vocabulary.
Plan and write a story with a beginning, a problem and an ending.
Proofread writing for spelling and punctuation errors and improve word choices.
Retrieve and record information from fiction and non-fiction texts.
Infer characters' feelings, thoughts and motives from their actions and justify with evidence.
Identify main ideas in a paragraph and summarise them in a sentence.
Work out the meaning of unfamiliar words from the surrounding text and check in a dictionary.
Read and discuss myths and legends, including one from the region they are visiting.
Prepare and perform a poem, using tone, volume and action to show meaning.
Write a simple poem about a place using imagery and repetition.
Use contents, headings, glossaries and indexes to find information.
Write a short persuasive piece, such as a leaflet for a place they visited.
Choose synonyms to make writing more precise and interesting.
Give a short, well-organised talk about something they have learned on their travels.
10-12: Use relative clauses beginning with who, which, where, when, whose or that.
Year 5 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Use modal verbs and adverbs to show degrees of possibility.
Year 5 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Use brackets, dashes or commas to add extra information (parenthesis).
Year 5 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Use semicolons and colons to link clauses and introduce lists.
Year 6 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Recognise and use the passive voice to change the focus of a sentence.
Year 6 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Recognise and choose formal and informal vocabulary and structures for different audiences.
Year 6 · Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Use adverbials and repeated ideas to link paragraphs smoothly.
Spell words with patterns such as -ough, -cious, -tial and silent letters.
Use Greek and Latin roots to understand and spell word families.
Use a dictionary and thesaurus efficiently to check meaning and find better words.
Identify and use similes, metaphors and personification.
Make inferences about characters and justify them with quotations from the text.
Why did the author write it that way?
Discuss how authors use language and structure to create effects on the reader.
Distinguish between statements of fact and opinion in articles, ads and travel reviews.
Compare two texts on the same theme, such as two descriptions of the same city.
Read and discuss an extract from a classic novel and its setting.
Read and discuss stories from other cultures, including the country they are visiting.
Explore how a poem uses form, rhythm and imagery to create meaning.
Write a narrative from a chosen character's point of view.
Use pacing, short sentences and setting details to build suspense.
Use dialogue to show character and move the action forward.
Write a travel article about a real place for a chosen audience.
Write an organised report with subheadings about a topic they have researched.
Research and write a short biography of a notable person from the region.
Write a balanced argument presenting both sides of an issue and a conclusion.
Plan and deliver a persuasive speech using rhetorical techniques.
Take part in a debate, listening and responding to others' points.
Summarise the main ideas from more than one paragraph in a short précis.
Proofread and redraft a piece of writing for clarity, accuracy and effect.
Read a news article and identify headline, angle, sources and audience.
13+: Read and interpret a scene from a Shakespeare play, focusing on language and character.
Analyse an extract of 19th-century fiction for setting, character and context.
Analyse a modern fiction extract and how the writer creates tone and voice.
Compare two poems on a shared theme, considering language, form and structure.
Explain how historical and cultural context shapes a text's meaning.
Select precise quotations and analyse the effects of specific word choices.
Analyse how writers structure texts to interest and guide the reader.
Compare how two non-fiction writers present different viewpoints on the same topic.
Identify and use rhetorical devices such as tricolon, anecdote and direct address.
Evaluate the reliability and bias of online sources and travel content.
Plan and write an analytical paragraph and essay using point, evidence and explanation.
Write a vivid, controlled description of a real place using varied sentence structures.
Write a short story using deliberate structure, such as flashback or a circular narrative.
Write an opinion article that argues a clear viewpoint for a specific audience.
Write a formal letter or email, such as a complaint or an enquiry, with an appropriate register.
Write a review of a place, book or film that balances description and evaluation.
Write a reflective travel memoir that connects events to personal growth.
Use simple, compound and complex sentences deliberately for effect.
Use dashes, semicolons, colons and ellipses accurately and for effect.
Use grammatical terms (clause, modal, subordinate, passive) when discussing writing.
Explore word origins and borrowings, including words English took from local languages.
Discuss how English varies by region and over time, and Standard English.
Draft, critique and redraft writing, explaining the improvements made.
Plan and deliver a formal speech or presentation with clear structure.
Take part in structured discussion, summarising and building on others' ideas.
Perform a scene, using voice and movement to interpret character.
Respond to a poem they have not seen before with a short analysis.
Read and discuss writing by an author from the region they are visiting, in translation if needed.
Research a topic using several sources, take notes and reference them.
Choose, read and review a full book independently, recommending it to others.
